Rules (machine-readable: `docs/status/release.yaml`). **RC3** is green only if (a) every vendor function that a streamer (timps, prudynt, raptor) calls works on T10, T20, T21, T23, T31, T40, T41 (API matrix cell dev, dev+, run, rt or vendor no-op), (b) no open issue has the label severity:critical or severity:high and (c) no open issue is in the milestone RC3. **Release 1:** RC3 is green and the release image ran at least 14 days on the fleet with at least 1 camera per SoC, 0 unplanned reboots and 0 oops; a new image or any reset restarts the counter; planned flashes and tests count as planned only when the camera STATUS log marks them so.

Project board status of an open issue (https://github.com/users/Lu-Fi/projects/1): Todo, In progress, **Monitoring** (diagnostics are running, waiting for the next event of the kind), **Waiting** (blocked from outside, for example on test hardware or a measurement setup; the issue says what it waits for, such as a light box A/B), Review, Done. Monitoring and Waiting issues are still open: they keep counting for the gates above.

## Summary

- **Update 2026-11-02 (night), #3 / #5 (T10/T20 `SetFisheyeEnableStatus` implemented as the vendor encoder's per-picture region of interest; API evidence: `Encoder_Get/SetFisheyeEnableStatus` T10/T20 cache -> dev; no feature symbol moved):** the vendor libimp 3.12.0 hands the flag to its encoder at CreateChn (i264e parameter 0x72); `i264e_icodec_enc` then clears the picture's ROI table (an application ROI is lost) and on IDR pictures and at every whole second of the frame rate codes the top-left 64x32 pixels at QP 15 or better. OpenIMP's T10/T20 build does the same (`src/fisheye`, docs/T20_FISHEYE.md). Proof: unicorn oracle of the vendor function (3815 cases, 0 differences), host test of the command list, QEMU T10 and T20, then the cameras with the vendor library and OpenIMP on the same camera: the same pictures carry the QP 15 region (IDR and each whole second; FixQP 30, FixQP 40, with an application ROI set), region QPs equal per picture (T10 100/100 in three scenarios, T20 99 to 100/100), streams decode clean (ffmpeg strict) with a real picture; 0 oopses, streamers restored. Differences: OpenIMP keeps the H.264 limit of 25 between neighbouring macroblock QPs (above slice QP 40 the region is raised), the T20 vendor CBR (macroblock rate control) limits the region to picture QP - 12 while OpenIMP's default CBR reaches 15. The ROI limit now counts from the slice QP when no macroblock QP table is active. The low-threshold CBR difference of the `SetChnDemask` runs (from picture 33 on) is the two rate controllers' QP trends on the same scene (the vendor QP falls faster after the first IDR), not the demask strategy, which equals the vendor for the same QPs; documented, not changed.
- **Update 2026-11-02 (afternoon), #3 / #5 (T10/T20 `SetChnDemask` implemented as the vendor's sharpness control loop; API evidence: `Encoder_Get/SetChnDemask` T10/T20 cache -> dev, `Get/SetChnH264Demask` and `Get/SetChnH264Denoise` n.a. -> dev as aliases; no feature symbol moved):** the vendor libimp 3.12.0 does not store the demask attribute: for every H.264 picture it compares the QP the encoder gave the previous picture with `demaskThresd` and steps the ISP sharpness by 0x14 per picture between 0x80 and 0 through `IMP_ISP_Tuning_SetSharpness_internal` (down while above the threshold with a hold of `demaskCnt` counts and a one-step hysteresis, up again afterwards; enable off restores the application's own sharpness). OpenIMP's T10/T20 build does the same (`src/demask`, docs/T20_DEMASK.md). Proof: unicorn oracle of the vendor setter, strategy and post-picture block (50 scenarios, 1300 pictures, 0 differences), QEMU T10 and T20, then the cameras with an LD_PRELOAD ioctl shim: the per-picture `VIDIOC_S_CTRL` sharpness calls of the vendor library and of OpenIMP on the same camera equal the strategy fed with the stream's QPs (T20 vendor 7/7, OpenIMP 7/7 scenarios; T10 vendor 7/7, OpenIMP 7/7), vendor against OpenIMP directly identical for the FixQP scenarios and the first CBR scenario (the low-threshold CBR one differs from picture 33 on with the rate controllers' QPs); streams decode clean with a real picture, snapshot 200, 0 oopses. `Fisheye` looked at (i264e_icodec_enc: with the flag the EFE ROI table is cleared every picture and on IDR pictures and whole seconds the top-left 64x32 pixels are coded at QP 15 or better), not implemented; stays open with `SetChnRcTrigLevel` and the HSkip second-try sizes.
- **Update 2026-11-02 (evening), #7 (T21 `SetChnHSkip` structures, `SetChnHSkipBlackEnhance` and scene-cut IDR coded; `Encoder_Get/SetChnHSkip` T21 dev with a new reference, `Encoder_SetChnHSkipBlackEnhance` T21 cache -> dev; `SetChangeRef` stays: no effect in the vendor either; API counts T21 works 301 -> 302 of 333, gaps 3 -> 2; no feature symbol moved):** the vendor libimp 1.0.33 has the T10/T20 reference-structure code, but honours it in SMART rate control only (`i264e_validate_parameters`), has no rate-controller class byte and no base-picture QP rule, three buffers for N1X/N2X, and never requests the SetChangeRef second try (proof by oracle: flag never set). OpenIMP's T21 encoder now does the same (`src/hskip`, `t30_helix_encoder.c`); the IDR period of N1X (`maxSameSceneCnt`) follows the SMART-only rule too. Proof: unicorn oracle with both vendor builds (76 x 240 pictures, validate 1680 cases, scene-cut IDR 36 x 240, black 635 sizes: 0 differences), encoder-level host test, QEMU T21, then the T21 camera against the vendor library on the same camera (FrameSource ch0 1080p, SMART): 0 differing pictures (NAL ref_idc, slice type, frame_num, list modification, MMCO, long-term flag) in 39 of 45 scenarios, the other 6 are scene-cut runs where only one library's base picture is larger than its last IDR picture; open streams decode clean (ffmpeg strict, VA-API) with a real picture, drop test clean, 0 oopses. Stays open: `Fisheye` (stored, no consumer identified), `H264TransCfg`, T21 `RcTrigLevel` (vendor no-op, documented in #7). docs/T21_HSKIP.md.
- **Update 2026-11-02, round 8 (evidence and notes only, no symbol moved: only device evidence for that SoC moves one; counts from the API coverage generator, per-bullet numbers below):** **#65 (closed)** T40 `SetAeAlgoFunc` / `SetAwbAlgoFunc` are device-verified with a measured effect on exposure and white balance and on by default (`OPENIMP_ISP_ALGO_FUNC=0` switches off); - **Update 2026-11-02 (night), #76 (T41 `SetAeAlgoFunc` device-verified, `SetAwbAlgoFunc` vendor no-op: err to dev / no-op, API evidence only, no feature symbol moved):** the vendor T41 libimp (1.2.5 / 1.2.6) uses the same callback protocol as T40 (ioctls 0xc004541b..e, one worker thread, notify after `SetSensorFPS`), so the T40 code (`src/t40/openimp_p1_algo.c`) now serves T41 too and the former ENOTSUP answers are gone. The stock T41 kernel module serves the AE commands (one channel) but has no AWB library ioctl at all (checked in the stock module and in the SDK firmware: no `tisp_awb_algo_init`, ioctls 0xc0045423..26 answer ENOTTY): with the vendor stack `SetAwbAlgoFunc` registers the record, the open at `EnableSensor` fails and the library is never called; OpenIMP does the same (cell no-op; a working AWB library would be beyond the vendor and is not built). The open-tx-isp T41 module got the AE path (translated `tisp_ae_algo_init/handle/deinit`, library woken by the vendor-AE statistics event). T41 test camera (runtime swap of the module, apitest case `customalgo_t41`, dead-man reset armed, stock module restored step by step): open 1 of 1, handle ~205 calls with statistics, notify 2 after `SetSensorFPS`, close 1 of 1; effect: a request of 9 lines read back as 9 in the ISP state and dropped the picture luma 65.4 to 26.4 (0.4x), 8x analog gain gave 8192 in the ISP state and luma 73.5, the base exposure again luma 66.3; after `DisableSensor` the internal AE controlled again on the same module instance. Regression with the module: apitest sys,fs,enc,osd,ivs,isp,su PASS 266 / FAIL 3 (the known AF statistics / metrics and LDC no-handler lines, as before), default cases PASS 164 / FAIL 0, WDR toggle and `SwitchBin` PASS, 6 of 6 reload cycles, 0 oopses, snapshot 200. QEMU T41 first (debug kernel with `slub_debug`, one CPU, fresh guest): three library sessions on one module instance, slab validate clean. Counts: T41 API works 364 to 366 of 427, gaps 12 to 10.
- **Update 2026-11-02 (later), #3 / #5 / #7 (T10/T20 `SetChangeRef` second try, `bEnableScenecut` and the base-picture QP coded; API evidence: `Encoder_Get/SetChangeRef` T10/T20 cache -> dev; no feature symbol moved):** the vendor libimp 3.12.0 codes a picture of the H1M classes (H1M_FALSE SBASE, H1M_TRUE LBASE) that its rate controller asks to code again (the SMART second try with ChangeRef on, also the super-frame re-encode) with the previous picture of the three-buffer ring as reference, keeps the smaller try and rewrites the header commands of a kept second try; base pictures take the QP of the last IDR picture (`i264e_decide_slice_qp`); with `bEnableScenecut` a base picture at a whole second that is larger than the last IDR picture is coded again as an IDR picture. OpenIMP now does the same (`src/hskip`, `t30_helix_encoder.c`). Proof: unicorn oracle (reference buffer, header commands, keep rule, QP rule, scene-cut decision: 76 scenarios x 240 pictures each, 0 differences), QEMU T20 and T10, then the cameras against the vendor library on the same camera: ChangeRef off and CBR streams identical, ChangeRef on with the same kinds of pictures as the vendor (T10: 7/8 and 9+12 against 7/8 and 9+12 list modifications; T20: the second try is kept for 9 to 10 of 21 base pictures, the vendor keeps all 21: the sizes of the two tries differ), the H1M_TRUE scene-cut IDR positions equal (0, 15, 45, 75), all OpenIMP streams decode clean (ffmpeg strict and VA-API) with a real picture while several vendor streams decode with errors; cameras and stock libraries restored, 0 oopses. Stays open: the SMART picture sizes of OpenIMP differ from the vendor's (QP trend of the drop-able pictures), `ChnDemask`, `H264Denoise`, T21 (the T21 library has the same i264e code; OpenIMP's T21 encoder has no skip structures yet).

- **Update 2026-11-02 (night), #65 (T40 `SetAeAlgoFunc` / `SetAwbAlgoFunc` device-verified: err to dev, API evidence only, no feature symbol moved):** on the T40 test camera (runtime swap of the open-tx-isp module, apitest case `customalgo_t40`) an AE library's result reaches the sensor (1/6 of the exposure time: picture luma 88 to 36, 4x analog gain: 133, the starting exposure again: 85, normal AE back after `DisableSensor`) and an AWB library's R/B gains move the picture chroma in the right direction (red gains Cb/Cr 112/197, blue gains 214/141) and are given back to the automatic white balance at `DisableSensor`. The calls are on by default now (`OPENIMP_ISP_ALGO_FUNC=0` switches off). Counts: T40 API works 336 to 338 of 389, gaps 13 to 11 (API coverage generator). - **Update 2026-11-02, #3 / #5 (T10/T20 `SetChnHSkip` structures and `SetChnHSkipBlackEnhance` implemented; API evidence only, no feature symbol moved):** the vendor libimp 3.12.0 (one binary for T10 and T20) codes the skip types as a reference structure (long-term base layer, drop-able pictures, IDR period of maxSameSceneCnt GOPs, T20 scene-cut IDR, all-skip black pictures); OpenIMP's Helix path stored the six words only. The three builds now run the T23 channel code with the software JPEG decoder (baseline JPEG, integer IDCT without libm, `OPENIMP_DECODER_SW_ONLY`): channel 0, JPEG into YUV420P / NV12 / NV21, `nrKeepStream` pictures in flight, oversized, non-baseline and damaged input refused with -1. Not equal to the vendor: speed (the VPU is faster) and the picture sits in a heap buffer without a physical address.

**Release candidate agg-34 (2026-10-09 evening, device results of the night 2026-10-09/10 added)**

- Final agg-34 after the review fixes (S1 T31 front crop survives the ISP session, S2 T31 zoom only with a scaled main stream, S3 Helix absolute ROI no longer worse than the slice QP): OpenIMP 2a1b1cd, open-tx-isp b15ef235 (test images with these on all 10 test cameras since 2026-10-09 night). The first state of the candidate was:
- State: OpenIMP `agg-34` (838f8147) = agg-32 (8980cae) + the encoder ROI clamp (fec3e69, 8545fb9) + the reviewed DeepSeek patches (11abe42 and 17 patches); open-tx-isp `agg-34` (da9baf1e) = agg-32 (3cf9bdac) + front-crop fixes for T31, T23, T20 and T10 (d940ba20 to 10bac52f, 164225e5) + T20 `isp-m0` reports the reachable analog gain cap (da9baf1e). The first release still covers T10, T20, T21, T23 and T31; T41 is experimental and not part of it.
- Soak of agg-32 (2026-10-07 16:07 to 2026-10-09 11:31, 43.4 h, stopped early by the user): 0 unplanned reboots, 0 oopses, 0 guard trips, 0 snapshot failures and no memory trend on the cameras without user interaction. The only reboots were a planned OTA and two crashes from enabling a front crop on T31 (fixed in agg-34, see below). The numeric picture check found the T20 day/night regression, the T10 black frame in the dark and the T41 channel-1 colour/exposure problem (known issues below).
- Encoder ROI (region QP): **T31** has an ROI that the vendor library does not have (`IMP_Encoder_SetChnRoiAttr` through the AVPU QP table, beyond vendor): device-tested, delta -10 gives 2.7x the bit rate, a relative -20 becomes -19 (clamped), 0 decoder errors in 20 VA-API checks; the night run of 2026-10-10 went through 20 phases (deltas, absolute QPs, clamp, off/on) with the stream valid in VA-API and in strict ffmpeg (`-err_detect`). Known deviation: under FixQP 42 a window of absolute 5 or relative -25 drives the P-frames to QP about 14 almost frame-wide (bit rate about x4, stream stays valid). **T10/T20/T21** apply `SetChnROI` on the Helix/NVPU: device-tested (T21 by default, beyond vendor); T20/T10 absolute ROI re-tested on 2026-10-10: valid H.264, no inversion (fix S3). All ROI paths now keep the stream valid H.264: every `mb_qp_delta` lies in -25..+25 (a relative -26 or an absolute QP far from the picture QP produced broken pictures in hardware decoders such as VA-API, VLC and browsers), picture QP plus delta stays inside the rate control's min/max QP. **T23**: regions on the native Helix encoder, device-tested on 2026-10-10 (QP map shows the window, streams valid in VA-API and strict ffmpeg). **T40/T41**: on by default since 2026-10-18 (T40 FixQP and CBR, T41 CBR/VBR only; no effect under FixQP on T41). Rules and numbers: `docs/ROI.md`, `docs/OPENIMP_BEYOND_VENDOR.md`.
- Front crop: **T10/T20/T21/T23** device-tested on 2026-10-09 after the fixes (T23: crop off unlocks the window, a window that does not fit is dropped instead of hanging the MSCA, the lock is released with the ISP session, module parameter `fcrop_upscale_pct`; T20/T10: a window set before stream-on is kept while no downscaled channel is open, is applied at stream on and survives substream restarts (device-tested 2026-10-10); the release of the window at tuning-session close is **not verified**). **T31**: the crash is fixed (the kernel refuses a window the MSCA would have to upscale with -EINVAL; scaler steps and latch are written; module parameter `fcrop_upscale_pct`); device-tested on 2026-10-10: a valid window zooms both streams (**proven**), too-small windows are rejected without a hang, and the window survives a restart and a flip.
- DeepSeek patches (17, reviewed, plus one corrected): struct sizes and layouts of the vendor ABI (T40/T41 encoder stream, channel attributes, frame info, sensor info, OSD attributes), encoder group bounds (6 like the vendor on T20/T21/T30/T31/T41, 8 kept on T23/T40), T31 IVS channel 64, `OSD_SetPoolSize(0)`, `GetDefaultBinPath`, idempotent IVS group create/destroy, polling-stream guards. Host tests and `make check` are green on all SoCs and the cross-builds pass; the combined agg-34 ran on the test cameras in the night 2026-10-09/10 (mandatory tests passed, streamer smoke on 9 cameras 50 of 50 without a `PollingStream` spin); not yet checked separately on cameras: OSD groups, IVS, T31 `SnapFrame` offsets and the T41 OSD size.
- T20 day/night: the driver reported an analog gain cap of 158 in `isp-m0` while the AE stops at 128, so a streamer waiting for the cap never saw it reached and stayed in Day mode in the dark. `isp-m0` now reports the smaller of the two: device-tested on T20 on 2026-10-10 (maximum analog gain 128). The streamer needs its matching change (timps 5bc4eff) for the switch to work; day/night with both is **not yet confirmed**. On T10 (jxh42) `isp-m0` still reports 144 at boot (128 once it is set explicitly): open finding.
- Streamer smoke test on 9 cameras (night 2026-10-09/10): 50 of 50 checks passed, no `PollingStream` spin (the streamer CPU stayed normal at stream restarts).

**Known issues (agg-34)**

- **T41 sub-channel (ch1):** green or flat frames at each day/night switch and the exposure of channel 1 does not follow channel 0 (channel 0 is fine). T41 is experimental and not part of the first release.
- **T20 day/night** needs the open-tx-isp fix (da9baf1e) **and** the streamer change (timps 5bc4eff); with agg-32 alone both T20 cameras stayed in Day mode in the dark. Not yet confirmed on a camera with both.
- **T10 analog gain cap:** `isp-m0` of the jxh42 camera reports a maximum analog gain of 144 at boot (128 once set explicitly); T20 reports 128 (fixed). Open.
- **ROI under FixQP:** with FixQP 42 an absolute 5 or relative -25 window lowers the P-frames to QP about 14 almost frame-wide (bit rate about x4); the stream is valid, but a streamer should not offer the extremes on a fixed-QP stream.
- **T20/T10 front crop:** the release of the window at tuning-session close is not verified.
- **T10:** the soak saw a few rounds where the camera switched to Day in the dark and delivered a black frame (3 events in 44 h).
- **720p main stream** shows only the top-left corner when the streamer reads `/proc/jz/sensor/sensor0/*` before the sensor is started (streamer side; seen on T21 and T20).
- **Streamer ROI limit:** the library keeps ROI streams valid H.264 from agg-34 on (a relative QP of -26 used to break Intel VA-API, VLC, Firefox and Edge from the ROI row on); a streamer that offers -26 should offer -25 as its lowest value.

**Release candidate agg-27/agg-28 (2026-10-06 evening; the apitest figures below are from that day)**

- State: OpenIMP `agg-27` (affb8ff) and open-tx-isp `agg-28` (79b754b4). Release plan: `next` goes to `aperto` (fast-forward) after the long soak, tagged `vYYYY.MM.DD`. The first release covers T20, T21, T23 and T31; T10 is part of it but was **not re-tested** on the open stack today (its cells mirror T20 and were not re-measured); T41 is **not** part of the first release (experimental, see below).
- Device results of the day (apitest, one call per vendor function; the camera streamer was stopped, the release libimp and the release-candidate modules were loaded from RAM): T20 on two cameras 212 PASS / 0 FAIL / 17 N/A / 30 SKIP, T21 on two cameras 228 PASS / 0 FAIL, T23 304 PASS / 4 FAIL (the four AF getters, off by default in that run; with the new default `source_af=1` they pass on a second T23 camera), T31 274 PASS / 1 FAIL (see known issues). N/A means the node or API does not exist on the board or in the vendor library (no RTC/ADC node, SU battery functions not exported, T20 `GetAeZone`, T23 `GetBlcAttr`), SKIP means the call is deliberately not exercised (writes hardware registers, reboot, cipher). 0 kernel oopses on every camera.
- What the code level "dev" means in the function tables below: the call passed apitest or imgfx on a camera of that SoC on 2026-10-06 (or an earlier documented device test). Cells of T10 were not touched by this run. The imgfx colour run of the release candidate was made in the dark (night mode), so its colour verdicts are not used; the colour image functions have to be repeated in daylight.
- New since the last matrix: `GetFrame`/`SnapFrame` wait up to 2 s like the vendor library on T20/T21/T23/T31 and the T20 capture no longer stalls (apps that call `SetFrameDepth` get frames); `Encoder_GetFd` (pipe plus pump thread); a JPEG channel feeds itself from the frame source when its video channel is not polled; two IVS groups; `InsertUserData` SEI; `PollingModuleStream` honours the channel bitmap; T20 encoder ROI and chroma QP offset; T21 `SetBrightness` acts and SEPIA works (both beyond vendor); T31 `SetFrameDrop` with the stock semantics; T23 release defaults (stock-like start/stop set, STREAMOFF drain wait), VBM pool parking and MSCA scratch buffer, AF statistics on by default, 19 ISP getters.
- Vendor no-ops that are matched, not "fixed": T21 `SetAntiFogAttr` and `SetSceneMode` (the OEM kernel accepts and ignores them), T20/T10 `GetAeZone` (the stock module does not serve the control), T23 `GetBlcAttr`/`SetScalerLv` (no handler in the stock module). T23 H.265 stays refused: there is no HEVC hardware (n.a.).

**Known issues of the agg-27 candidate (older; superseded where agg-34 says so)**

- **T23 crop hang:** the pipeline stops after a FrameSource crop change (hard hang, found with the crop test); under investigation. It is a release blocker. **Fixed in agg-34** (open-tx-isp 25b1d8c7, 164225e5; device-tested on T23, retest on the release image pending).
- **T31 H.264 stalled after the JPEG channel was torn down:** fixed: two threads polled the same encoder channel at once (`AL_Codec_Encode_Process` concurrently); `IMP_Encoder_PollingStream` now serialises per channel (openimp `claude/release-fix27` 5c2ccef), apitest on T31 FAIL 0 with the fix; goes into the next candidate (agg-29).
- **T41 is not part of the first release:** MSCA channel 1 scaling registers are staged only (a downscale above 4:1 gives garbage, buffers with index 1 and above show a band), a restart of the output hangs the SoC (watchdog reboot at 1280x720 / 1440x810 on channel 1), 38 tuning IDs are still missing (gamma, CCM, CSC, module control, auto zoom, manual exposure, DRC, DPC, defog ratio, mask, scaler level), flip is not reset on restore, the FIFO delay of the frame source is missing. The T41 branches `claude/release-t41` (OpenIMP) and `claude/t41-ch1-fix` (driver) are not merged. T41 apitest on that branch: 255 PASS / 12 FAIL.
- **T21:** the IPU needs about 2 s after a wake before the OSD blend takes effect; the first snapshot is withheld until the overlay is confirmed (beyond vendor), the cause is not found. The OSD in the live stream after a wake is checked after the candidate tests.
- **T23:** the sporadic Helix encode error (errno 5): 0 errors in 6 days on cam-B since the 0102 fix (syslog: 342, 32, 37 and 419 errors on 10-01..10-04, then 0 from 10-05 to 10-10); provisionally closed, still observed; no real WDR, as before.

**What is complete**

- All five original test cameras (cam-A T31, cam-B T23, cam-C T20, cam-D T21, cam-E T10) run fully on the open kernel driver, OpenIMP and timps from flashed images; cam-F (T41) runs the same stack from the `aperto` full OTA image; no Ingenic/neo helper libraries any more, and on T23 no helixd and no vendor libimp either.
- Core functions are backed by evidence: H.264 on all six SoCs (soaks up to 2 h 53 without errors), HEVC on T31, hardware JPEG/MJPEG, second stream, OSD (text, bitmap, rectangle, line), real motion detection, day/night, flip.
- Beyond the vendor: reload/stop robustness (0 oops in 10 cycles each), smaller libimp (~0.5–0.6 MB instead of 1.0–1.3 MB), more free video memory on T21 (2.76 MB instead of ~1.2 MB), T31 module smaller than vendor, T21 controls and noise reduction take effect (the vendor ignores them), T31 AEC with −18 dB echo, reference-frame sharing on T21/T23 (~1.5 MB less video memory, on by default).

**Open items from 2026-10-04** (still valid unless the release-candidate section above says otherwise)

- T23: the frequent Helix frame drops had a fixed cause (a residual interrupt treated as an error by the bounded-wait kernel patch; 60 min with 0 errors after the fix); the sporadic single encode error (errno 5): 0 errors in 6 days on cam-B since the 0102 fix (syslog: 342, 32, 37 and 419 errors on 10-01..10-04, then 0 from 10-05 to 10-10); provisionally closed, still observed. Real WDR is missing (dynamic ADR is lifted, no WDR sensor mode).
- T41 (cam-F): runs the fully open stack with H.264 (main stream High 1080p ok) and H.265; AE compensation, gain/exposure caps and 2D noise reduction work through OpenIMP; DRC, DPC, defog, WDR, CCM, gamma, HLC and BLC are not supported on T41 (the driver says so). ## Legend

- ✅ supported: works, matches vendor behaviour, tested or backed by the changelog
- ✅+ improved beyond vendor: more robust, leaner or more functional than the vendor stack
- ⚠️ known defect / deviation: runs, but with a known defect or a deviation from the vendor
- 🔧 in progress: branch is running or a test is pending
- 📋 planned: deliberately scheduled, not started yet (mostly low priority)
- ❌ missing: not implemented
- — hardware does not have it: not applicable
- ? unknown: not documented in the sources, deliberately not guessed
- [-all-13]: historic tag (tested before the later aggregates); everything so tagged is contained in `next`

Columns T10..T41 (T30 and T40 added 2026-10-10): one status symbol per SoC (legend above). The number and the feature name link to the detail section below, which holds the full per-SoC text and the vendor-stack behaviour.

**T30/T40 columns added 2026-10-10.** Evidence basis: host and build evidence only. There is no T30 camera in the lab, so no T30 cell is better than 🔧 (code present, or a live result documented by the T30 contributor in `docs/T30_STATUS.md`, not repeated by us) and nothing is ✅. T40 cells rest on the branch `claude/t40-t41-api` (merged into agg-35, not yet in `next`) and, since 2026-10-10, on the cam-K device run: host tests, the cross-build and the exported symbols of its libimp.so, plus the T40 contributor's live gate in `docs/T40_STATUS.md` (2026-07-30, stock `tx_isp_t40` driver). **T40: first OpenIMP device run on cam-K (2026-10-10)**: T40XP board, vendor kernel driver `tx_isp_t40`, vendor libimp 1.3.0, OpenIMP loaded via `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`; every T40 result is OpenIMP versus the vendor library; the cells that run as dev are exactly the functions listed in the update paragraph at the top. The rest stays host or `?`. `?` = nothing documented or only an exported symbol without a test; `—` on T40 = the call does not exist in the T40 1.3.1 vendor headers. Camera letters: none for T30 (no camera); cam-K = T40 (T40XP). The function tables below hold the per-call detail.

### Matrix details

Per feature: the vendor-stack behaviour and the full per-SoC cell text (chronological test log, newest results win).


#### ISP core and image pipeline

##### 1. ISP core / sensor bring-up

- **Vendor stack:** tx-isp-*.ko loads sensor + tuning bin
- **T10:** ✅ open driver boots, boot guard auto; day/night 10x without oops
- **T20:** ✅ bring-up stable; vendor-format isp-m0
- **T21:** ✅ first open bring-up, ISP core = lifted vendor code
- **T23:** ✅ exposure readback live, ~45 empty CIDs wired up, unknown CIDs return -EINVAL
- **T30:** 🔧 open-tx-isp T30 core builds against a T30 kernel and had a hardware bring-up earlier (open-tx-isp README); the T30 contributor ran the ISP + FrameSource path live (`docs/T30_STATUS.md`); not run by us (no T30 camera)
- **T31:** ✅ reference SoC; tuning gaps closed (RGB coefficients, AE ROI, SensorAttr)
- **T32:** 🔧 QEMU only, no camera: open-tx-isp `driver/t32` reaches AddSensor to EnableTuning in the QEMU T32 image (stages S1-S3), driven by the vendor libimp 2.2.0; no OpenIMP T32 build yet (T32NQ test module ordered)
- **T33:** 📋 planned, not started: no T33 driver, OpenIMP build or hardware yet (T33L test module ordered)
- **T40:** ✅ 2026-11-01 (#150, device-tested on the Eufy .184): the pipeline-top block `main` is zeroed at ISP open like the vendor (all 31 registers read 0 after open, they kept the hardware defaults 0x200/0x22/2/2 before); the `sec` block keeps its defaults on both stacks; the value stays 0 over 6 reload cycles, 0 oopses. Earlier: 2026-10-24 (Eufy .184, agg43c): the oops at every `S95timps start` is fixed: a stack overflow in `tx_isp_core_ops_s_ctrl` (the antiflicker SET copied 8 bytes over a 4-byte OEM stack slot and smashed the saved register of the caller, BadVA 0x4890) and in `video_s_stream` (`255a46ff`, `f981c6a2`); the IQ bin path now comes from the registered sensor name (`91f41ac7`); with the SDK patch for the Eufy sc830ai 2-lane mode the camera streams 1080p20 from the 4K sensor continuously and survives a second timps start (open-tx-isp next 2c29ce79; the sensor patch itself is firmware-side). Earlier (history): device-tested 2026-10-10 on cam-K (T40XP; vendor kernel driver `tx_isp_t40`, vendor libimp 1.3.0 side by side, OpenIMP via `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`): `AddSensor`/`EnableSensor`, `ISP_Tuning_GetSensorAttr` and `GetCameraInputMode` run like on the vendor library (OpenIMP vs vendor); the T40 contributor's live gate in `docs/T40_STATUS.md` (2026-07-30). Vendor note: `GetAeExpList` hung the vendor kernel driver; the magenta cast seen with timps stopped was the IR cut left open, not the library. Open driver (`tx_isp_t40`, Eufy sc830ai 4K) since 2026-10-12: devtest 24/35 results with 0 failures, 300 s and 10-min stream runs, 0 oops (2026-10-15..19)
- **T41:** ✅ 2026-10-27: `SetDefaultBinPath` before `AddSensor` works (#116: the 132-byte T41 record, the open driver loads the given file instead of the sensor's default bin; T41 camera AddSensor 0 instead of -1), `SetISPBypass` sends its ioctl as soon as the ISP device is open like the vendor and the driver refuses the real bypass (value != 0, returns -1) until its VIC capture path works (#125; the real bypass is a long-term item). Earlier: runs the fully open stack from the `aperto` full OTA image since 2026-10-04; defaults since 2026-10-19: vendor AE per frame, OEM CLM and per-frame tone worker, 16.6 h overnight soak on .32 without reboot or oops (2026-10-18/19)

##### 2. Reload / error handling (rmmod, stop/start)

- **Vendor stack:** known oops on reload (T21 open counter, stats DMA)
- **T10:** ✅+ boot guard auto; reload cycles not documented individually
- **T20:** ✅+ rmmod during stream rejected; 10x stop/start + 10x reload, 0 oops; all 53 user copies checked
- **T21:** ✅+ 10x stop/start + rmmod/insmod, 0 oops; cause of the old oops (stats DMA into freed memory) fixed
- **T23:** ✅+ 2026-11-02 (#189 pass 5, T23 test camera, full OTA of a new image; vendor-compared triage of the lifted entries): 22 reachable lifted functions triaged (3 fixed, 19 dead because the hand-written layer replaces them or nothing dispatches them); `ispcore_core_ops_ioctl` is now a hand-written event walk with a host test. Default image: apitest all areas PASS 420 / FAIL 11 (the image before, same session: 399 / 32; no function worse, 11 remaining FAILs were FAILs before: 10 second-sensor getters and `SetScalerLv`), 6 of 6 module reload cycles, 3 RTSP pulls, 6 day/night switches, 0 oopses. No visible effect expected or seen for the event walk (no sender of these events in the live code). The two other fixes (`jz_isp_ccm`, `tisp_ae_mean_update`) are reached only with the bring-up parameter `source_core_start=0`; that mode resets the camera within seconds on this tree and on its parent alike (cause not explained, pre-existing), so they have no camera-verified effect. Earlier: 10x stop/start incl. kill -9, 10x reload, 0 oops; 2 out-of-bounds writes (2 KB/18 KB) fixed
- **T30:** 🔧 2026-11-01, QEMU only (no T30 camera, no cell moves above QEMU level): the audit fixed three driver faults in the QEMU T30 machine: `GetSensorRegister` no longer oopses (#174), the second FrameSource channel start no longer oopses in the ISP interrupt (the multi-scaler push FIFO is cleared at stream-off like the vendor, 45 cycles clean, #175) and the ISP init interrupt window is gated (#176). The issues stay open until a T30 camera confirms them. Earlier: 2026-10-25: reaches the driver in QEMU (T30 image, sc4236 model; reload/controls clean after six driver fixes), no T30 camera. Earlier: ? not documented
- **T31:** ✅+ 10x reload with kill -9; vmalloc leak of 252 KB/cycle fixed; residual drift ~45 KB/cycle
- **T32:** ? not examined: no T32 hardware yet; the open driver only runs in QEMU and OpenIMP has no T32 build
- **T33:** 📋 planned, not started: no T33 driver, OpenIMP build or hardware yet (T33L test module ordered)
- **T40:** ✅+ 2026-11-01, round 7 (#189, class `postret`: 25 lifted functions where the MIPS delay-slot statement ended up behind the `return`, 14 of them on T40, restored and vendor-compared; Eufy T40 camera, image agg65m): apitest all areas PASS 398 / FAIL 0, area t40dev 82 PASS / 0 FAIL, 6 planned module reload cycles clean, 0 oopses, snapshot 200. Wording: the functions are not instrumented, so 'reached' means the apitest area that drives that code path ran clean, not a verified effect of the restored store; the AE exposure numbers equal the run before. T30 `mem_write_u32` is not run on a camera (host only). Earlier: 2026-11-01, typed-pointer audit (#189, Eufy T40 camera, image agg65k = open-tx-isp next with the 11 fixed lifted functions: CSI/ISP/VIN slake and activate, tuning-node open, FrameSource and sensor ioctls, sub-device pipo, VIC frame-done lists, `__frame_channel_vb2_streamoff`, msca state init): a scanner in `make check` finds lifted code that steps typed pointers (byte offsets multiplied by the element size); the fixes ran on the camera clean: apitest all areas PASS 398 / FAIL 0, area t40dev 83 PASS / 0 FAIL, 11 FrameSource disable/enable cycles, 6 planned module reload cycles (module use count back to the same value each time, slab flat), about 25 minutes of streaming, snapshot 200, 0 oopses. Reached by those paths; not instrumented per function. Not proven on the camera: the 21-count wait loop of `__frame_channel_vb2_streamoff` (no buffer stayed pending) and the DVP leg of `tx_isp_vic_start` (no DVP camera); #189 stays open for the remaining suspects and T41. Earlier: 2026-11-01 (Eufy T40 .184, images agg65b to agg65f, open-tx-isp next with #150, #152, #182, #183): the clock teardown at rmmod follows the vendor: every enable of an ISP or CSI clock is counted and what is left is gated after the last child removal (#152); after each unload `div_isp`, `gate_isp` and `gate_csi` read 0 and the ISP clock gate bit is off (before: the counts grew by one per load), the sensor module stops its own MCLK. 6 planned reload cycles per image, 0 oopses, snapshot 200 after every reload; apitest all areas PASS 398 / FAIL 0 / N/A 24. The oopses found on the way are fixed with device proof (WDR-enable/LCE arrays #182, draw-attribute NULL dereference #183, AWB close with the algorithm callbacks on #173). QEMU ingenic-t40: 22 load/unload cycles with a running streamer. Earlier: Update 2026-10-24, evening (open-tx-isp `claude/t40-reload`, merged): reload and restart are clean now, the 'staying ⚠️' reasons below are overtaken. The first unload oopsed in the frame-channel removal (a lifted `wake_up_all(NULL)`, the fault the vendor `tx_isp_t40` shows on rmmod and that QEMU reproduces); the frame source is now removed before the core, the objects the lift had turned into `kfree(NULL)` are freed, `/proc/jz/isp` and the sensor I2C client are released, the lifted `vmalloc` areas are freed at exit and the per-session leak (about 36 areas / 344 KB per streamer restart, the vendor frees them per session) is closed. Eufy T40 (.184, test module, then stock restored): 10 reloads, 10 `kill -9` + reload, 10 streamer restarts = 30/30 cycles, snapshot 200 every time, 0 oopses, unloaded `vmalloc` and kernel memory flat. ✅+ because the vendor module oopses on rmmod. Older text: 2026-10-24 reasons for staying ⚠️ (code audit, camera busy): the 10-10 oops (epc 0x6ef, module size 763904) was the VENDOR `tx_isp_t40`; the open module was rmmod-tested twice on 2026-10-13, exit steps 1-8 fine, step 10 (core platform device remove) took the SoC down (2nd time without watchdog recovery, power cycle) and it has not been rmmod-tested since. Current next: exit is split into 15 steps (`echo exit N > /proc/tx_isp_t40_recovered` for a bisect), the core remove skips `ispcore_slake_module` by default (`t40_rmmod_skip_slake=1`, untested) and `tisp_deinit` is skipped (`skip_tisp_deinit=1`, tisp allocations probably leak per load); `tx_isp_core_remove` has no NULL check of drvdata and both OEM kfree calls are `private_kfree(NULL)`. Next: per-step bisect with the flight recorder when the Eufy is free (needs power-cycle permission). Status before: the stop/start path (second `S95timps start` after the bind fix) is clean. Earlier (history): 2026-10-24: after the bind fix a second `S95timps start` on the same boot is clean (no oops), agg43c, 2026-10-24. Earlier (history): 2026-10-18: 10/10 ch0+ch1 stop/start cycles after the OEM release reset on the last `/dev/tx-isp` close (`claude/t40-restart-hang`, 181/181 frames each), 5 client reconnects, 0 oops (T40_RESTART_HANG_1018); rmmod/insmod cycles are not run (the test state is a reboot between runs); MemFree drifts about -0.5 MB over 10 sessions (open)
- **T41:** ✅+ 2026-11-01, round 7 (#189, 21 retyped lifted functions plus 5 `postret` fixes; Cinnado T41NQ test camera, image agg5y = open-tx-isp next with both sets, `t41_af` at its default off): apitest areas sys,fs,enc,osd,ivs,isp,su PASS 266 / FAIL 3 (AF statistics, AF metrics and LDC answer 'no handler': AF block off by default, no LDC), a real WDR on -> off toggle read back, SwitchBin day and night, 13 FrameSource disable/enable cycles, 7 planned module reload cycles (slab flat), 0 oopses, snapshot 200. Wording: reached by that code path, not instrumented per function. Not exercised: the DVP leg of `tx_isp_vic_start` (MIPI camera), suspend/resume functions (no power management on the board), `api_ae_set_exprinfo_attr` (no default case calls it) and `tisp_msca_ch_curve_write` (non-default scaler curve): host/compile only. Earlier: 2026-10-24 on .34 (Cinnado sc5336, image agg4x, open-tx-isp next `2c29ce79`), all in ONE boot (uptime 1:38 at the end): 31 module unload/load cycles (10 after a normal streamer stop, 10 with `t41_heap_watch=1 t41_heap_decoys=32`, 10 after `kill -9` of the streamer without DelSensor) plus 10 streamer stop/start and 8 kill -9 restarts = 49 cycles, every snapshot 200, 0 oops, 0 hangs, 0 heap-watch/decoy hits (the 10-12 build hit a decoy in 10 of 50 cycles), the `bad vinum` / `csi init invalid` guards never fired; unloaded vmalloc 26 entries flat, MemFree with no trend, SUnreclaim +3 kB/cycle without diagnostics (noise), sensor i2c client gone after every unload, module refcount 0, streamer RSS 2.9-3.7 MB flat. Beyond the vendor: the vendor `tx-isp-t41` leaks the `tisp_top` page at every stream start and keeps a stale sensor i2c client after a streamer crash; the open driver frees the page (`tisp_deinit`) and releases the client on unload or before the next register. Caveat: the writer of the 10-12 heap overwrite is not named, only its two possible paths are closed (`688ba69a`, `67200912`, `57449bdb`). Earlier (history): 2026-10-23 RC2 run on .32 (gc5603): one module reload (streamer stopped, `rmmod` sensor + `tx_isp`, `insmod` with the image defaults) rc 0, CLKGR as after boot, streaming and snapshot fine, then 9 reboots in total (6 + 3), back in 27-32 s each, snapshot 200 after 40 s, 0 oops. The 17-cycle module-parameter heap bug (#2 below) was not re-run, so the cell stays ⚠️. Earlier (history): rev2 image: 10/10 rmmod/insmod cycles OK, refcnt 0, 0 oops; kill -9 of the streamer recovers 3/3; the boot oops (kthread_stop -EINTR, use-after-free of `isp_fw_process`) is fixed (`claude/t41-boot-oops`, 2026-10-17). Open: the module-parameter heap overwrite across reloads (oops in the 17th load/unload cycle, 2026-10-12; named again as "rmmod heap bug" in the 2026-10-19 size audit)

- **Vendor stack:** not present
- **T10:** ✅+ isp_open=auto
- **T20:** ✅ S10isp-guard + isp_open=auto: optional package in upstream thingino `aperto` (#1749, default off); active on the test cameras
- **T21:** ✅+ S10isp-guard, u-boot isp_open=manual|auto|off
- **T23:** ✅ S10isp-guard + isp_open=auto: optional package in upstream thingino `aperto` (#1749, default off); active on the test cameras
- **T30:** ? not documented
- **T31:** ✅ S10isp-guard + isp_open=auto: optional package in upstream thingino `aperto` (#1749, default off); active on the test cameras

  Earlier: ✅ 2026-10-24 (third pass): the defog diamond lattice is fixed and defog is **on by default** (`t41_defog=1`, open-tx-isp `cfdd1420`/`091e1fa2`, user decision 2026-10-24). Root cause: the translated defog chain read its constant tables from the rodata image of the vendor-AE translation (15760 B) instead of the rodata of the reference module it was translated from (14784 B); the tables sit at different offsets, so `defog_count_weight35abc` scaled garbage into the curve and weight-table registers and the saturated-weight zone showed as a bright diamond at every block corner. Now the defog registers 0xc000..0xc28c on .32 (gc5603, 2880x1620, bright light) are identical to the vendor dump (0 differences, before 64); diamond metric -0.7 on / -0.9 off (before +8..+18); contrast std +7.5 %, Laplacian +10 % with defog on; `defog_irqs == frames`, no oops. `Module_Ratio` index 4 acts (0..255). **Not tested:** the strength sweep (`SetDefog_Strength`, the OpenIMP branch `claude/t4x-defog-strength` is not merged; a timps control does not exist) and a haze scene; the API ratio sweep of 2026-10-23 stays the only strength evidence. Earlier (history): The OEM defog chain is translated and runs per frame (`bbd103fb`, `defog_irqs == defog_frames` about 25/s, no storm), the module accepts the defog ratio of `Module_Ratio` index 4 (the old -EOPNOTSUPP answer is gone). Device test on .32 (2026-10-23, `imgfx_t41` ratio sweep, same scene, no brightness shift): block luma std 15.5 / 16.3 / 16.8 / 23.2 at ratio 0 / 64 / 128 / 255, so the effect is measurable at 255 and small below 128; `SetModule_Ratio` returned an error word for 0/64/255 although the value was applied (return-code quirk, open). **Default is OFF since 2026-10-24** (`t41_defog=0`, `af9b3519`): the defog stage left diamond artefacts in the picture in the A/B runs. The timps `image.defog_strength` control still says "not supported"; `IMP_ISP_Tuning_SetDefog_Strength` for T40/T41 (`claude/t4x-defog-strength`, host tests only, vendor has no such call) and the haze scene test are not merged, so the cell is 🔧 and not ✅. T40: no defog call in the vendor library.

Earlier (history): 2026-10-24 on .32 (gc5603, open stack, full-size 2880x1620 frames, manual AE, scene mean Y about 52, not fully black; `tests/t41/dpcscan.c` counts pixels brighter than all 8 neighbours, d>=24 / d>=48): default 91/15, DPC bypass 189/26, ratio 0 195/36, ratio 128 45/6, ratio 255 54/8, i.e. DPC on halves the isolated-peak count (2.1-4x fewer), ratio 255 about equal to 128; the API returns 0 with readback (default 128, vendor default 128). Open: the default (unit disabled) and an explicit ratio 128 differ in run 1 (91 against 45 peaks) but lie within the noise in run 2 (AE/order effect); a re-test in a fully dark slot with more frames is running, so the cell stays ⚠️ until it is decided. The formulas are the decompiled stock `tisp_s_dpc_ratio`, equivalence to the vendor by code, not measured (no vendor image). Earlier (history): the DPC ratio unit of `Module_Ratio` is implemented in the driver (long-bank thresholds scaled from the pristine table, `6fcf5502`) and the tone worker interpolates the DPC gain per frame; no device measurement of the effect (host/build only)

##### 45. Encoder ROI (region QP)

- **Vendor stack:** `IMP_Encoder_SetChnROI` (T10/T20/T21/T23), `IMP_Encoder_Set/GetChnRoiAttr` (T40/T41); no ROI API in the T31 library
- **T10:** ✅ regions on the Helix/NVPU, device-tested; absolute QPs are limited to the valid H.264 range; absolute ROI re-tested 2026-10-10: valid, no inversion
- **T20:** ✅ regions and H.264 chroma QP offset, device-tested (QP 51 region blocky, QP 15 clean); valid H.264 from agg-34 (an absolute QP more than 25 from the macroblock QP broke hardware decoders before); absolute ROI re-tested 2026-10-10: valid, no inversion
- **T21:** ✅+ effective by default (beyond vendor: the vendor never programs it), device-tested; relative QP acts inside -12/+13 of the slice QP; `OPENIMP_T21_ROI=0` switches it off
- **T23:** ✅ on the native Helix encoder (default backend), the same registers the vendor 1.3.0 encoder programs; device-tested 2026-10-10: QP map shows the window (relative QP acts inside -12/+13 of the slice QP, like T21), bit rate +10 % at delta -15 and -4 % at +20/absolute 51, 9 streams valid in VA-API and strict ffmpeg; OPENIMP_T23_ROI=0 switches it off
- **T30:** ? ROI calls (4 vendor names) exported, no test result for T30
- **T31:** ✅+ beyond vendor: `IMP_Encoder_Set/GetChnRoiAttr` through the AVPU macroblock QP table (H.264 only), device-tested: delta -10 gives 2.7x the bit rate, a relative -20 is clamped to -19, absolute 51 blurs the region, 0 decoder errors in 20 VA-API checks; 2026-10-10: 20 phases valid in VA-API and strict ffmpeg (`-err_detect`); known deviation: under FixQP 42 an absolute 5 or relative -25 window drives the P-frames to QP about 14 almost frame-wide (bit rate about x4, stream valid); `OPENIMP_T31_ROI=0` refuses the call
- **T32:** ❌ no OpenIMP T32 build yet (the function would need one); no T32 hardware yet
- **T33:** 📋 planned, not started: no T33 driver, OpenIMP build or hardware yet (T33L test module ordered)
- **T40:** ✅ `Encoder_Get/SetChnRoiAttr` (10 windows, AVC only) through the same AVPU macroblock QP table as the T31 (one byte per 16x16 block in EP2, cmd[9] bits 25/24; the vendor 1.3.1 library builds the same one-byte table and sets the same bits); **on by default** since 2026-10-18 (`OPENIMP_T40_ROI=0` refuses the call); device-tested on the Eufy T40XP in FixQP and CBR (FixQP 32 window -20: 100 to 1194 kbit/s, CBR window +20 drops the window SSIM 0.96 to 0.89); `SetChnMapRoi` is still not exported on T40
- **T41:** ✅+ 2026-10-24 ROI also works under FixQP (beyond the vendor: the vendor library shows no ROI effect under FixQP on T41, capture of libimp 1.2.6). Cause of the old limit: the vendor pins the QP range word EP2 header +0x10 (max<<24 | min<<16 | 0x302) to QP..QP under FixQP (0x1e1e0302 at QP 30) and the AVPU clamps every macroblock QP to it. `avpu_t41_roi_apply` opens the range to 0x33000302 while a window or map is active and restores the pinned word afterwards (the HWRC words are not needed). Device (.32, 1280x720 15 fps FixQP 30, window 384x240 at 448,240): window -20 raises P-frames from 222 to 2364 B and the bit rate from 431 to 977 kbit/s, window +20 gives window SSIM 0.79 against 0.93 away from it, whole frame -20 gives 19 Mbit/s, `SetChnMapRoi` -20 432 -> 1023 kbit/s and +20 window SSIM 0.75 against 0.98; ROI off restores the stream (IDR 84578 against 84573 B base). CBR/VBR: path unchanged, on by default (2026-10-18: whole frame -20 doubles the bit rate, a +20 window drops its SSIM 0.97 to 0.73; vendor CBR +20: window SSIM 0.84 against 0.98 away). `OPENIMP_T41_ROI=0` refuses the call. Not clean: an open-stack CBR re-run was confounded by a scene change and .32 rebooted once during a further CBR run while another job reloaded the module on the same camera (cause unknown). Earlier (history): `Encoder_Get/SetChnRoiAttr` (AVC) through the AVPU QP table with cmd[152] bits 0 and 3 as the vendor sets them; **on by default for CBR/VBR** (device-tested 2026-10-18 on Cinnado .34 and Vanhua .32: whole frame -20 doubles the bit rate, a +20 window drops its SSIM 0.97 to 0.73); (then) under FixQP the AVPU ignored the table (cause found 2026-10-24, see above); `OPENIMP_T41_ROI=0` refuses the call; `SetChnMapRoi` rides on the same switch (not device-tested)
- **Rules (all SoCs with ROI):** window deltas -25..+25; spread of all deltas at most 25; picture QP plus delta inside 0..51 and the rate control's min/max QP; requests beyond that are clamped with a one-time warning (`SetChnRoiAttr` returns -1 for a delta outside -26..25 or an absolute QP outside 0..51)

<details><summary>Notes and references (60)</summary>

- `ISP_SetAeAlgoFunc`: T40: vendor protocol ported (SetAe/AwbAlgoFunc keep the callback record, EnableSensor registers it with ioctl 0xc004541d / 0xc0045425 and starts the worker, workers ioctl 0xc004541b/c and 0xc0045423/4, DisableSensor closes with 0xc004541e / 0xc0045426, SetSensorFPS notifies the AE library). On by default, OPENIMP_ISP_ALGO_FUNC=0 switches it off (-1 / ENOTSUP). Device-verified effect (#65, T40 test camera, apitest customalgo_t40): the AE callback result reaches the sensor: a request of 1/6 of the running exposure time (1919 -> 319 lines) read back as 319 lines in the ISP state and dropped the picture luma 88 -> 36 (0.4x); a 4x analog gain request (4095 in the ISP state) raised it to 133; the starting exposure requested again gave 85; after DisableSensor the normal AE came back (1800 lines, same gain and luma 120 as before). | T41: needs a user-space callback thread fed by the ISP module (ioctl 0xc004541d); the open T41 module runs its own AE and has no such event path; OpenIMP exports the call as -1/ENOTSUP (apitest case t41isp PASS in QEMU T41) T41 (#76, 2026-11-02, T41 test camera .34, runtime swap of the open-tx-isp module, apitest customalgo_t41): same libimp protocol as T40 (the vendor T41 libimp 1.2.5/1.2.6 uses the same ioctls 0xc004541b..e), served by the stock T41 dispatcher commands and by the open module since #76 (translated tisp_ae_algo_init/handle/deinit, library woken by the vendor-AE statistics event, one channel). Reached: open 1 of 1, handle ~205 calls with statistics, notify 2 after SetSensorFPS, close 1 of 1. Verified effect: the library's integration time 56 -> 9 lines read back as 9 in the ISP state and the picture luma dropped 65.4 -> 26.4 (0.4x), 8x analog gain at 9 lines gave 8192 in the ISP state and luma 73.5, the base exposure again gave luma 66.3; after DisableSensor the internal AE controlled again on the same module instance. Needs an open-tx-isp T41 module with the #76 path (older modules answer ENOTTY: the record is registered, the open fails with a message). T41: QEMU T41 2026-10-31 case t41isp. T40: apitest customalgo_t40 on the T40 test camera 2026-11-02 (runtime swap of the open-tx-isp module, dead-man armed): customalgo_ae_effect_t40 and customalgo_awb_effect_t40 PASS (numbers in the note), open/close 1 of 1, handle ~190 calls each, 0 oops; regression with the module: apitest all areas PASS 398 / FAIL 0, t40dev 0 FAIL, 6 of 6 reload cycles, 0 oops.
- `ISP_SetAwbAlgoFunc`: T40: vendor protocol ported (SetAe/AwbAlgoFunc keep the callback record, EnableSensor registers it with ioctl 0xc004541d / 0xc0045425 and starts the worker, workers ioctl 0xc004541b/c and 0xc0045423/4, DisableSensor closes with 0xc004541e / 0xc0045426, SetSensorFPS notifies the AE library). On by default, OPENIMP_ISP_ALGO_FUNC=0 switches it off (-1 / ENOTSUP). Device-verified effect (#65, T40 test camera, apitest customalgo_t40): the AWB callback result changes the white balance: r x2 / b x0.5 moved the picture chroma (Cb/Cr) from 172/171 to 112/197, r x0.5 / b x2 to 214/141, the start gains again gave 161/159, and the gains the ISP reported followed each request exactly; DisableSensor gave the automatic white balance back (manual gains 0). | T41: needs a user-space callback thread fed by the ISP module (ioctl the AWB twin of 0xc004541d); the open T41 module runs its own AWB and has no such event path; OpenIMP exports the call as -1/ENOTSUP (apitest case t41isp PASS in QEMU T41) T41 (#76): vendor no-op - the stock T41 module has no AWB library ioctl (0xc0045423..26 are not in its dispatcher; the SDK firmware has tisp_awb_algo_deinit but no tisp_awb_algo_init), so with the vendor stack SetAwbAlgoFunc registers the record, the open at EnableSensor fails and the library is never called; the open stack does the same (apitest customalgo_t41 on the T41 test camera: open 0, handle 0, close 0, frames flow). A working AWB library on T41 would go beyond the vendor. T41: QEMU T41 2026-10-31 case t41isp. T40: apitest customalgo_t40 on the T40 test camera 2026-11-02 (runtime swap of the open-tx-isp module, dead-man armed): customalgo_ae_effect_t40 and customalgo_awb_effect_t40 PASS (numbers in the note), open/close 1 of 1, handle ~190 calls each, 0 oops; regression with the module: apitest all areas PASS 398 / FAIL 0, t40dev 0 FAIL, 6 of 6 reload cycles, 0 oops.

QEMU T30 (sc4236 model, no camera): FAIL (ISP_Tuning_AE_GetROI: ret=-1 roi 0x00000000). - `Decoder_*`: T10/T20/T21: the vendor libimp (T10/T20 3.9.0 and 3.12.0, T21 1.0.33) exports all eight calls and decodes JPEG in the VPU (ijpegd, a decoder channel thread); OpenIMP decodes in software in the calling thread (baseline JPEG, own integer IDCT, no libm), same API: channel 0, JPEG into YUV420P/NV12/NV21, nrKeepStream pictures in flight, picture in a malloc buffer (no physical address). Device: a 1080p picture takes about 2 s on T20/T21 and about 1 s for 720p on T10 (the VPU is faster); pictures above maxWidth x maxHeight, non-baseline files and damaged data are refused with -1. | T40: declared in imp_decoder.h, exported by no vendor library; OpenIMP exports the names as -1/ENOTSUP from the shared T40/T41 code, so nothing is missing. | T41: the vendor JPEG decoder is not in the T41 1.2.5 libimp; OpenIMP exports the eight names as -1/ENOTSUP without touching anything (src/t40/t4x_unbound.c). apitest case dec: 8/8 PASS in QEMU T41 T41: apitest agg5y 2026-11-01 .34 (open-tx-isp next a84b6be2 + OpenIMP next 246bf938, full-order cases run): 8/8 PASS, every call -1/ENOTSUP, arguments untouched, frames still flow. T40: vendor libimp T40 1.3.1 (uclibc and glibc libimp.so, libimp.a): no IMP_Decoder_* symbol exported (nm -D, strings); the names only exist in the SDK header imp_decoder.h, so the stock library answers a program with an unresolved symbol (checked 2026-10-31, #66). T10: apitest dec-t1x 2026-11-01 .31 (library from /tmp, streamer restarted, stock module md5 unchanged): 8/8 PASS (32 PASS / 0 FAIL in the case run; QEMU T10 first: 8/8, frames flow); a JPEG snapshot of the same camera (1280x720) decoded to NV12 against a host decode of the same file (ffmpeg): Y PSNR 68.8 dB, SSIM 0.9999, max difference 1 level, chroma PSNR 63.8 dB. T20: apitest dec-t1x 2026-11-01 .107 (library from /tmp, streamer restarted, stock module md5 unchanged): 8/8 PASS (32 PASS / 0 FAIL; QEMU T20 first: 8/8, frames flow); JPEG snapshot of the same camera (1920x1080) decoded to NV12 in 2.0 s against a host decode of the same file: Y PSNR 69.5 dB, SSIM 0.9999, max difference 1 level, chroma PSNR 60.7 dB. T21: apitest dec-t1x 2026-11-01 .24 (library from /tmp, streamer restarted, stock module md5 unchanged): 8/8 PASS (32 PASS / 0 FAIL; QEMU T21 first: 8/8, frames flow); JPEG snapshot of the same camera (1920x1080) decoded to NV12 in 2.0 s against a host decode of the same file: Y PSNR 69.0 dB, SSIM 0.9999, max difference 1 level, chroma PSNR 62.5 dB.

- `Encoder_Get/SetChangeRef`: T10/T20: stored and read back with the vendor return codes (SetChangeRef -1 on an idle channel, GetChangeRef -1 on an idle channel; apitest PASS on T10, T20); T21 (2026-10-10, host test): SetChangeRef -1 on an idle channel; GetChangeRef answers 0 on an idle channel and, as the vendor (T21 1.0.33 and T30 1.0.5, same code), logs "unsupport to change ref channel" and returns -1 on every created channel without writing the value (it used to return the stored value); the vendor passes it to the i264e reference code (param 12), which only the HSkip reference modes read; the Helix path codes no HSkip structure (class c). Disassembly: T21 1.0.33 0x48bd4/0x48d90, T20 3.12.0 0x4b05c/0x4b220; T30 1.0.5 (same vendor code as T21): SetChangeRef stores the flag of a created channel (-1 for an idle one); GetChangeRef is 0 for an idle channel and -1 for a created one (the vendor logs "unsupport to change ref channel"); host test; T30 1.0.5 (same vendor code as T21): SetChangeRef stores the flag of a created channel (-1 for an idle one); GetChangeRef is 0 for an idle channel and -1 for a created one (the vendor logs "unsupport to change ref channel"); host test T10/T20: stored and read back with the vendor return codes (SetChangeRef -1 on an idle channel, GetChangeRef -1 on an idle channel; apitest PASS on T10, T20); T21 (2026-10-10, host test): SetChangeRef -1 on an idle channel; GetChangeRef answers 0 on an idle channel and, as the vendor (T21 1.0.33 and T30 1.0.5, same code), logs "unsupport to change ref channel" and returns -1 on every created channel without writing the value (it used to return the stored value); the vendor passes it to the i264e reference code (param 12), which only the HSkip reference modes read; the Helix path codes no HSkip structure (class c). Disassembly: T21 1.0.33 0x48bd4/0x48d90, T20 3.12.0 0x4b05c/0x4b220; T30 1.0.5 (same vendor code as T21): SetChangeRef stores the flag of a created channel (-1 for an idle one); GetChangeRef is 0 for an idle channel and -1 for a created one (the vendor logs "unsupport to change ref channel"); host test; T30 1.0.5 (same vendor code as T21): SetChangeRef stores the flag of a created channel (-1 for an idle one); GetChangeRef is 0 for an idle channel and -1 for a created one (the vendor logs "unsupport to change ref channel"); host test. T30 audit 2026-11-01 (OpenIMP claude/t30-audit, #24): Exported by the T30 1.0.5 vendor libimp and by OpenIMP's T30 build. QEMU T30 (sc4236 model, no camera): FAIL (Encoder_GetChangeRef: ret=-1 ChangeRef = 0; Encoder_SetChangeRef: ret=0 ChangeRef set 1, read back 0). Documented T30 limitation: the value is not read back by the Helix encoder path (apitest expects the T20 stored value). T10/T20 2026-11-02: the flag is coded: a picture of the H1M classes that the rate controller asks to code again (SMART second try with the flag on; any re-encode of those pictures) is coded again with the third reconstruction buffer as reference, the smaller try is kept and a kept second try gets the vendor header commands (i264e_get_prev_fram_dec 0x42940, i264e_ratecontrol_is_reenc_end 0x4d474, i264e_dec_ref_pic_remark 0x42a24, i264e_slice_write 0x46cb0); tests/hskip (76 scenarios x 240 pictures against the vendor code), see docs/T20_HSKIP.md. T10 reads the flag only when the controller is set up, T20 with every picture. T21 2026-11-02: no effect in the vendor either: the second-try flag (picture+0x1284) is cleared by i264e_ratecontrol_is_reenc and never set (its only writer, i264e_ratecontrol_is_reenc_end, is called with the flag already set), i264e_decide_slice_qp is an empty function and the ChangeRef parameter is read by no controller code; tools/t21_changeref_oracle.py runs the vendor judge for 6952 calls with ChangeRef on and off: flag never set, no decision depends on it (docs/T21_HSKIP.md). Camera: ChangeRef on/off 0 differing pictures against the vendor libimp. T21: hskip 2026-11-02 .24 vs the vendor libimp 1.0.33 on the same camera: SetChangeRef on/off identical streams in structure (0 differing pictures), as the vendor has no second try on T21 (oracle: flag never set over 6952 judge calls); apitest agg63 2026-10-31 .24. T23: apitest agg47 2026-10-26 .30. T30: FAIL apitest t30audit 2026-10-31 QEMU (no camera): Encoder_GetChangeRef: ret=-1 ChangeRef = 0; Encoder_SetChangeRef: ret=0 ChangeRef set 1, read back 0. T10: changeref 2026-11-02 .31: per-picture structure vs the vendor library on the same camera (SMART H1M_FALSE / H1M_TRUE, flag on and off, CBR): 7 / 8 list modifications against 7 / 8 (H1M_FALSE), 9+12 against 9+12 (H1M_TRUE); strict ffmpeg decode clean (the vendor streams decode with 4 to 16 errors), 0 oopses. T20: changeref 2026-11-02 .107: per-picture structure vs the vendor library on the same camera (SMART H1M_FALSE / H1M_TRUE, flag on and off, CBR): flag off and CBR identical, flag on: the kept second try carries no list modification (9 to 10 of 21 base pictures against 21 of 21 of the vendor: the second try must be smaller, the picture sizes differ); strict ffmpeg and VA-API decode clean, real picture, 0 oopses.

CreateChn hands the flag to the encoder as i264e parameter 0x72 and its only reader is i264e_icodec_enc (0x4d740): with the flag the ROI table of every coding try is cleared (an application ROI is lost) and on I slices and at whole seconds of the frame rate (counter * fps_den % fps_num == 0) region 0 is set to the top-left 64x32 pixels at absolute QP min(slice QP, 15). OpenIMP's T10/T20 build does the same (src/fisheye, docs/T20_FISHEYE.md). Proof: unicorn oracle of i264e_icodec_enc (3815 cases, 0 differences), host test of the command list (region 0 programmed on IDR and whole-second pictures only), QEMU T10 and T20, cameras with the vendor library and OpenIMP on the same camera: the pictures that carry a macroblock at QP 15 or better are the same (IDR and every whole second; FixQP 30, FixQP 40, with an application ROI set, which the flag removes), and the region macroblocks' QPs are equal per picture (T10 100/100 in all three, T20 100/100 with the ROI and at QP 40, 99/100 at QP 30; the long T20 runs of 225 pictures: 14 of 15 whole-second pictures in OpenIMP, 15 of 15 in the vendor); streams decode clean (ffmpeg strict) with a real picture, equal to the vendor's statistics. Differences: OpenIMP keeps the H.264 limit of 25 between neighbouring macroblock QPs (an IDR at slice QP 45 gets its region at QP 20, the vendor writes QP 15, a step that ffmpeg hides); T20 CBR: the vendor's macroblock rate control limits the region to the picture QP - 12, OpenIMP's default CBR has no macroblock table, so the region reaches 15; a region whose macroblocks are all skipped shows no QP in the stream (the missing 1 of 15). - `Encoder_SetbufshareChn`: vendor T31 1.1.6 / T40 1.3.1 / T41 1.2.6 (disassembled): stores the share channel in the channel record (kept over CreateChn, set to -1 by DestroyChn; a negative value is valid and means no sharing) and CreateChn reads it for a JPEG channel only: the JPEG channel borrows the video channel's stream manager and stream contexts and skips building its own pool of stream buffers (CreateChn fails when that video channel does not exist yet; T41 also refuses the MMA option). OpenIMP: same value handling, argument checks and return codes (-1 on T31/T40, 0x80040001 on T41, both channel numbers below the channel limit); CreateChn only logs a warning where the vendor would fail. There is nothing to share: OpenIMP JPEG channels own no stream buffer pool (JPEG is software on T40/T41, T31 uses one hardware-JPEG stream buffer for all JPEG channels), so sharing would save no rmem; measured on a T40 camera (video 640x360 plus a JPEG channel in the same group, with and without the call): JPEG channel cost about 24-72 kB of free memory either way, snapshots valid, H.264 decodes without errors in software and VA-API decoders. - `SU_Base_SetWkupMode`: T41: the board's neo-sysutils writes the mode into /sys/power/state (the kernel refuses it); the vendor libsysutils 1.2.5 opens /dev/rtc0 and sends ioctl 0x80045209 with {0, 0x2c, 0xd2ad2d28 (mode 1) / 0xd2ad2d29 (mode 2)}. OpenIMP's libimp.so now exports the vendor request (src/core/su_base_wkup.c, host test with fake open/ioctl; QEMU T41: mode 0 refused by libimp.so, modes 1/2 never sent: they arm an RTC wake-up). Camera run needed: ls -l /dev/rtc0, then mode 1 once with the result of the RTC driver T41: host test tests/core/su_base_wkup_test.c; QEMU T41 2026-10-31 mode 0 refusal.
- `SU_Base_Shutdown`: agg-37: OpenIMP exports it in `libimp.so` on every SoC (sync, then SIGTERM to init = reboot by default; `OPENIMP_SU_SHUTDOWN=poweroff` sends SIGUSR2, `=vendor` the vendor SIGCHLD); host test with a fake kill, not run on a camera.
